title: Running away to Milwaukee: Slick's Palm Garden and the John Wheeler band
summary: Howard leaves Chicago with John Wheeler's band for Slick's Palm Garden, gets his first long-pants tuxedo, and the sign reading 'Jazz Band' is replaced with 'Ginger Band'.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I said, no. It felt like it was doing like that. Yeah, it was funny. Yeah. This band, you see, they introduced me to running from home. Because I couldn't work here, nobody did know me in Milwaukee. And it was the first long pantsuit I ever had in my life. We got off the train and they waited for the pawn shop to open. Went in there and bought me a long, a first long pantsuit. It was a tuxedo. I can't stand them today. Yeah. Well, you went to Milwaukee. At Slick's Palm Garden. With his band. John Wheeler's Ginger Band. You were 12? So that was. No, I was 14 then. That'd be 1920. I was 12 years old. I was 12, not all. 18. 1918. 1918. Great. Nice. They had a sign up. John Wheeler's Jazz Band. Great name of the red letters. J-A-S-S-E. And so they made them take the sign down, see. And they finally replaced it with John Wheeler's Ginger Band. No kidding.
You mean the word jazz had a bad comment.

It looked like they had A-S-S on there instead of Chris, it should have been A-Z-Z, you know. Yeah. But the man didn't want it up there no kind of way since they hadn't made that first mistake, you know. That's crazy. So where'd you go when you ran away from home? Milwaukee. For how long? Well, we played at the Slick's Palm Garden for nine months and went from there to Minneapolis.
